userStories.title: Flow permission keys, catalog risk, activity entity
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Register the flow permission vocabulary, human approval floor, developer grants, approval ask component and activity entity.

**Motivation** — Every later piece (steps, verdicts, merge waits, the flow page, nax's send-to-koda tool) needs the record, its states and its approval first.

**Approach** — Verbatim design notes:
- **Human floor.** `fleet.flow.start` is classified `critical` in `classifyRisk`, so its approval floor and default are `human` and no policy can lower it: an agent can never approve a flow.
- **Humans only for the tick, in the route.** `fleet.thread.preapprove` keeps `principals: ['user', 'agent']`: a user-only catalog entry would make every role holding it (`developer`, and `project-admin` through `*`) unbindable to agents (`RoleAdminService.assertPrincipalType`). The pre-approval route commands refuse a non-USER actor with 403 `fleet.flows.humanOnly` instead.
- **Developer role.** `developer` gets `fleet.flow.create`, `fleet.flow.stop`, `fleet.flow.start` and `fleet.thread.preapprove` explicitly; it already holds `fleet.flow.read` through `*.read`.
Permission catalog target: `NEW_KEY_SCOPES` adds `fleet.flow.read`, `fleet.flow.create`, `fleet.flow.start`, `fleet.flow.stop`, `fleet.thread.preapprove` (all `'project'`) and `system.flow.respec` (`'any'`); `classifyRisk` returns `critical` for `fleet.flow.start`; `PENDING_SURFACE_KEYS` adds all six, and each later story removes the key it declares (`fleet.flow.start` stays: no route declares it, as with `fleet.budget.override`).
Update catalog.spec.ts's separate NEW_KEY_LIST, risk table and derive helper, regenerate the role-matrix snapshot, and append flow after provider_credential in the activity entity closed-world test. Add flow to ASK_KEYS_BY_COMPONENT without altering other component mappings.

**Scope** — In: catalog, seeded developer grants, role-matrix snapshot, approval component mapping and activity entity vocabulary. Out: models/state rules (US-002), command registration (US-005), actual human-only tick enforcement (US-008), declared routes/listener and their pending-key removals (US-008 to US-012).

**Interface** — `ASK_KEYS_BY_COMPONENT` target adds `flow: 'fleet.flow.start'`; `FLEET_ENTITY_TYPES` target ends `provider_credential, flow`. Preserve `findCatalogEntry`, `ApprovalPolicyResolver.resolve` and `RoleAdminService` public APIs.

userStories.title: FleetFlow schema, migration and state rules
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add durable flow/feature records, nullable advance thread approval, domain contracts and pure lifecycle rules.

**Motivation** — Every later piece (steps, verdicts, merge waits, the flow page, nax's send-to-koda tool) needs the record, its states and its approval first.

**Approach** — Verbatim data model:
```prisma
model FleetFlow {
  id                String    @id @default(cuid())
  projectId         String
  repoId            String
  threadId          String?
  entry             String    // THREAD | NAX
  createdByType     String    // USER | AGENT
  createdById       String
  branch            String
  specSha           String
  pinnedRunnerId    String?
  reviewerRole      String
  supervisorRole    String
  costCapUsd        Decimal   @db.Decimal(12, 4)
  spentUsd          Decimal   @default(0) @db.Decimal(12, 4)
  state             String    @default("PENDING")
  approvalMode      String?   // REQUEST | PRE_APPROVED
  approverId        String?
  approvedAt        DateTime?
  approvalRequestId String?
  stopReason        String?
  endedAt           DateTime?
  createdAt         DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime  @updatedAt
  project           Project   @relation(fields: [projectId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  repo              FleetRepo @relation(fields: [repoId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  features          FleetFlowFeature[]
  @@index([projectId, createdAt])
  @@index([threadId, state])
  @@index([repoId, branch, specSha])
  @@index([approvalRequestId])
}

model FleetFlowFeature {
  id           String    @id @default(cuid())
  flowId       String
  position     Int
  feature      String
  specPath     String
  dependsOn    String[]
  state        String    @default("PENDING")
  currentStep  String?
  prNumber     Int?
  flow         FleetFlow @relation(fields: [flowId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  @@unique([flowId, position])
  @@unique([flowId, feature])
}
```
`ChatThread` gains `preApproval Json?`, shape `{ userId: string, at: string (ISO), costCapUsd: string }`, surfaced on `ChatThreadRecord` as `preApproval: ThreadPreApproval | null`. US-004 implements that record mapping. Add Project/FleetRepo back-relations and additive migration 20261125090000_fleet_flows; use local constants/types rather than Prisma enums.

Verbatim flow-state contract:
`FleetFlowState`: `PENDING`, `APPROVED`, `RUNNING`, `WAITING_MERGE`, `WAITING_ANSWER`, `COMPLETED`, `STOPPED`. Pure `canTransitionFlow(from, to)`:
| from | allowed to |
|:---|:---|
| PENDING | APPROVED, STOPPED, PENDING (re-ask) |
| APPROVED | RUNNING, PENDING, STOPPED |
| RUNNING | WAITING_MERGE, WAITING_ANSWER, COMPLETED, STOPPED, PENDING |
| WAITING_MERGE | RUNNING, STOPPED |
| WAITING_ANSWER | RUNNING, PENDING, STOPPED |
| COMPLETED | (none) |
| STOPPED | (none) |
`isLiveFlowState(state)` is true for every state except `COMPLETED` and `STOPPED`. F1 itself moves flows only along PENDING -> APPROVED, PENDING -> PENDING (re-ask), PENDING -> STOPPED, APPROVED -> PENDING and APPROVED -> STOPPED. A feature row's `state` is `PENDING` at creation; F3 owns its other values. Stop reasons written by F1: `approval_rejected`, `human_stop`.

**Scope** — In: schema, migration, domain types/repository token and pure rules. Out: repository implementation (US-003), thread mapping/mutations (US-004), approvals (US-005). Dispatching any job (spec review, PLAN, PRD review, RUN, REVIEW, FIX, finish); F1 creates, approves and stops records only. Single-feature steps, the cost cap check between jobs, `spentUsd` accumulation and job-failure stops (fleet flow F3).

**Interface** — `canTransitionFlow(from, to)`; `isLiveFlowState(state)`; domain token `FLEET_FLOW_REPOSITORY`; domain repository contract for create with features, findById, lockById, findPage({ projectId }), findLiveForThread, findLiveForSpec, approve, reask, updateSha and stop, implemented by US-003.

[unit] canTransitionFlow('PENDING', 'RUNNING') returns false.
[unit] canTransitionFlow('COMPLETED', 'PENDING') returns false.
[unit] canTransitionFlow('STOPPED', 'APPROVED') returns false.
[unit] isLiveFlowState returns true for PENDING, APPROVED, RUNNING, WAITING_MERGE and WAITING_ANSWER.
[unit] isLiveFlowState returns false for COMPLETED and STOPPED.
[integration] After migrating, inserting a FleetFlow row with only the required columns stores state PENDING and spentUsd 0.
[integration] Inserting two FleetFlowFeature rows with the same flowId and feature fails with Prisma error code P2002.
[integration] Inserting a ChatThread row without preApproval stores it as null.

[integration] Applying migration 20261125090000_fleet_flows to a database with an existing published ChatThread preserves that row's publishedSha, specPublished, runnerId and maxCostUsd while its new preApproval is null.

userStories.title: FleetFlow repository
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist and query ordered flow features and enforce flow transitions under row locks.

**Motivation** — Every later piece (steps, verdicts, merge waits, the flow page, nax's send-to-koda tool) needs the record, its states and its approval first.

**Approach** — Verbatim story target: `PrismaFleetFlowRepository` extending `AbstractPrismaRepository`: create with features, `findById`, `lockById`, `findPage({ projectId })`, `findLiveForThread`, `findLiveForSpec(repoId, branch, specSha)`, and transitions `approve`, `reask`, `updateSha`, `stop`, each locking the row and checking `canTransitionFlow`.
Verbatim design notes:
- **Live flow.** Every non-terminal state (not `COMPLETED`, not `STOPPED`) is live. One live flow per thread (thread row lock) and per `(repoId, branch, specSha)` on the nax entry (`FleetRepo` row lock).
- **Lock order.** Thread row (`ChatThread ... FOR UPDATE`) or `FleetRepo` row, then flow row (`FleetFlow ... FOR UPDATE`), then the request through `close`. Every flow transition reads the state under the flow row lock and checks `canTransitionFlow`.
Use the existing transaction proxy and parameterized SQL lock precedent from the provider credential repository. Atomic nested create must leave no parent after feature uniqueness failure. Assign zero-based positions and always include features sorted by position. findPage filters projectId and returns Nathapp pagination with newest-first ordering. Live queries use isLiveFlowState's nonterminal contract. approve records mode, approverId, approvedAt and request id; reask updates sha/request, clears previous approval mode/user/time; updateSha preserves all approval attribution and changes no lifecycle state; stop records reason/time and rejects terminal transitions with FlowTransitionError. For an unchanged state such as approved updateSha, do not treat a metadata-only write as an invalid APPROVED -> APPROVED transition. Parent serialization is the create service's responsibility, not a new global uniqueness restriction on terminal history.

**Scope** — In: repository implementation and transaction/ordering/transition behavior. Out: parent-lock orchestration, asks and audit/activity (US-007/US-011/US-012), module registration (US-005), HTTP authorization/routes (US-008 to US-011).

**Interface** — `findLiveForSpec(repoId, branch, specSha)`; `approve(flowId, { mode: 'REQUEST', approverId, approvedAt, approvalRequestId })`; `reask(flowId, { specSha, approvalRequestId })`; `updateSha(flowId, specSha)`; `stop(flowId, 'human_stop', now)`; `findPage({ projectId })`. Implement the US-002 domain repository contract and preserve full flow/feature data.

[integration] findById returns the features in position order with their dependsOn arrays.
[integration] create with two features of the same name throws and leaves no flow row.
[integration] findLiveForThread(threadId) returns the thread's flow in APPROVED.
[integration] findLiveForThread(threadId) returns null when the thread's only flow is STOPPED.
[integration] findLiveForSpec(repoId, branch, specSha) returns a PENDING flow with those three values.
[integration] approve(flowId, { mode: 'REQUEST', approverId, approvedAt, approvalRequestId }) sets state APPROVED and the four approval columns.
[integration] reask(flowId, { specSha, approvalRequestId }) on an APPROVED flow sets state PENDING, stores the new sha and request id, and clears approvalMode, approverId and approvedAt.
[integration] updateSha(flowId, specSha) on an APPROVED flow changes only specSha.

[integration] stop on a STOPPED flow throws FlowTransitionError and leaves the row unchanged.

userStories.title: Thread pre-approval data and the guarded thread lock
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose thread advance approval and add thread-owned locked operations that flow creation can safely call.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, merged #392) turns a settled spec set into ready PRs with one approval.

**Approach** — Verbatim design notes:
- **Thread data through `ThreadsService`.** The flows module never reads the thread repository. `ThreadsService` gains `lockForFlow(projectId, threadId)`, which takes the thread row lock and applies the thread-entry guards in the Failure Handling order (it owns `threadsEnabled`), plus `setPreApproval`, `clearPreApproval` and `consumePreApproval`.
- **The tick has no expiry and no spec binding.** It is the user's advance approval (design G4) for whatever the thread publishes next, up to its cap; it is consumed by the first flow it covers.
- **Thread responses show the tick.** `ThreadDto` gains `preApproval { userId, at, costCapUsd } | null` so the F6 control can render it; the tick is not secret.
`ChatThread` gains `preApproval Json?`, shape `{ userId: string, at: string (ISO), costCapUsd: string }`, surfaced on `ChatThreadRecord` as `preApproval: ThreadPreApproval | null`.
Verbatim story target: `ChatThreadRecord.preApproval`, its mapping and `ThreadDto.preApproval`, and the `ThreadsService` methods `lockForFlow`, `setPreApproval`, `clearPreApproval`, `consumePreApproval` with their repository methods. `setPreApproval` and `clearPreApproval` lock the thread row and audit under `fleet.thread.preapprove`; `consumePreApproval` writes no audit (the flow create audits).
lockForFlow requires the caller's transaction and checks in order: project-scoped missing -> 404 threads.notFound; non-REPO -> 409 threads.notRepoThread; disabled -> 409 threads.disabled; archived -> 409 threads.archived; unpublished -> 409 threads.notPublished; missing runner -> 409 threads.runnerMissing. It does not impose thread.plan ownership. Ticking is advance approval, so set/clear do not require a published spec or runner. A no-op clear returns false and writes no audit. Map null on old rows, update typed record/repository fixtures and publish the nullable Swagger shape in ThreadDto; regenerate openapi.json using bun run api:export-spec.

**Scope** — In: thread domain/repository/service/DTO and additive OpenAPI field. Out: flow consumption eligibility and Decimal comparison (US-007), actor rejection and gated HTTP tick routes (US-008), publish events (US-012). Pre-approval expiry or binding the tick to a published sha: by design the tick approves in advance whatever the thread publishes, up to its cap, and is consumed by one flow.

**Interface** — `lockForFlow(projectId, threadId): Promise<ChatThreadRecord>` (inside the caller's transaction: thread row lock, then the guards, throwing their errors), `setPreApproval(projectId, threadId, userId, costCapUsd)`, `clearPreApproval(projectId, threadId): Promise<boolean>` and `consumePreApproval(threadId)`.

userStories.title: Flow input validation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Parse both flow entry bodies into one bounded, normalized feature/role/cap contract.

**Motivation** — nax's G5 `nax-flow__send` is built against this feature's create endpoint, so F1 ships the nax entry now instead of last.

**Approach** — Verbatim design bounds:
- **Bounds.** 1-20 features; feature names follow `FEATURE_RE` (`^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]{0,127}$`) and are unique; `specPath` 1-300 characters, relative, ends `.md`, no `..` segment; `dependsOn` names only features listed earlier, no duplicates; role values 1-200 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:/\[\]=,-]`; `costCapUsd` greater than 0, at most 1000, at most 4 decimal places; `branch` matches `GIT_REF_RE`; `specSha` is 40 lowercase hex.
- **Remote URLs.** `remoteUrl` accepts what `parseGitHubUrl` accepts (`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>[.git]`); its `skills.unsupportedHost` error is rethrown as a validation error naming `remoteUrl`.
Verbatim API bodies: Thread-entry body: `{ features: [{ feature, specPath, dependsOn? }], roles: { reviewer, supervisor }, costCapUsd }`. nax-entry body: the same plus `{ remoteUrl, branch, specSha }`. Pre-approval body: `{ costCapUsd }`.
Implement pure parseFlowInput(body, entry) using the shared FEATURE_RE/GIT_REF_RE rather than reimplementing a different branch/name grammar. Normalize missing dependsOn to [], preserve caller order and validate each dependency against previously accepted feature names. Name the exact failing property (features, features.0.feature, features.0.specPath, features.1.dependsOn, roles.reviewer, roles.supervisor, costCapUsd, branch, specSha or remoteUrl) in ValidationAppException. Do not perform DB or forge work. Return JSON-serializable normalized cap data that can be parsed again when an approved route command executes. The role character class must allow the bracketed role/model syntax exactly as specified.

**Scope** — In: pure flow parser and property-specific failures. Out: HTTP gate/permission checks (US-008 to US-011), forge head/path checks (US-010), tick storage (US-004), duplicate detection (US-007).

**Interface** — `parseFlowInput(body, entry)` in `flow-input.ts`; thread and nax shapes above; failure is `ValidationAppException` naming the property.

userStories.title: The flow create service
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Create either flow entry through one transaction that prevents live duplicates and either requests human start approval or consumes a covering tick.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, merged #392) turns a settled spec set into ready PRs with one approval.

**Approach** — Verbatim algorithm:
`FleetFlowsService.create(input, creator, context)` runs in one transaction: take the thread lock (`lockForFlow`) or the `FleetRepo` lock; refuse a live flow on the thread, or a live duplicate on the nax entry; insert the flow and features; consume a covering tick (`APPROVED`, `PRE_APPROVED`) or open the `fleet.flow.start` ask and store its id; audit `fleet.flow.create`; record `flow.created`. Each create route's `routeCommand.run` calls it.
Verbatim design notes:

- **Thread data through `ThreadsService`.** The flows module never reads the thread repository. `ThreadsService` gains `lockForFlow(projectId, threadId)`, which takes the thread row lock and applies the thread-entry guards in the Failure Handling order (it owns `threadsEnabled`), plus `setPreApproval`, `clearPreApproval` and `consumePreApproval`.
- **Thread entry trusts the thread's publish record.** Thread publish commits to a ref in the runner's local clone and never pushes, so koda cannot read thread-entry specs from the forge. - **Who consumes a tick.** A tick covers a flow whose creator is the tick's user or the thread's creator; a flow created by anyone else on that thread is `PENDING`. Covered means the tick's cap is at least the flow's cap, as decimals.
- **Live flow.** Every non-terminal state (not `COMPLETED`, not `STOPPED`) is live. One live flow per thread (thread row lock) and per `(repoId, branch, specSha)` on the nax entry (`FleetRepo` row lock).

**Goal** — Accept nax flow proposals using a reachable registered GitHub repository and verified branch-head spec snapshot.

**Motivation** — nax's G5 `nax-flow__send` is built against this feature's create endpoint, so F1 ships the nax entry now instead of last.

Inside `run`, under the `FleetRepo` row lock, the duplicate check and the create.
- **Remote URLs.** `remoteUrl` accepts what `parseGitHubUrl` accepts (`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>[.git]`); its `skills.unsupportedHost` error is rethrown as a validation error naming `remoteUrl`.
- **Every write route is gated.** The write keys are approvable, and the permission contract refuses an ungated write that requires one (`ungated-approvable-write`). Each write route runs through `routeGate.run` with a registered route command; for a human, or an agent with no policy asking, it executes at once; an agent whose policy asks gets 202 with the request, and approving it runs the command.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose project-scoped list/detail and agent-reachable detail, plus an approval-gated terminal stop operation.

**Motivation** — Every later piece (steps, verdicts, merge waits, the flow page, nax's send-to-koda tool) needs the record, its states and its approval first.

**Approach** — Verbatim story target: `ProjectFlowsController`: `GET /api/projects/:slug/flows`, `GET /api/projects/:slug/flows/:flowId` and gated `POST /api/projects/:slug/flows/:flowId/stop`; `GET /api/fleet/flows/:flowId` on `FleetFlowsController` with the read enforced in the flow's project. Verbatim design notes:
- **Every write route is gated.** The write keys are approvable, and the permission contract refuses an ungated write that requires one (`ungated-approvable-write`). Each write route runs through `routeGate.run` with a registered route command; for a human, or an agent with no policy asking, it executes at once; an agent whose policy asks gets 202 with the request, and approving it runs the command.
- **Request id on the flow.** The flow row stores `approvalRequestId`; no `FleetApprovalAsk` link row. Asks are closed with status `cancelled` and reason `superseded` or `flow_stopped`; `close` returns null when a decide holds the request, and the `approvalRequestId` guard then makes the late decision a no-op. `execute` reads `requestId` and `approverId` from the action context with a local helper (as `FleetBudgetOverrideCommand` does); `onReject` receives no request and reads only `currentContext().approval.requestId`.
- **Lock order.** Thread row (`ChatThread ... FOR UPDATE`) or `FleetRepo` row, then flow row (`FleetFlow ... FOR UPDATE`), then the request through `close`. Every flow transition reads the state under the flow row lock and checks `canTransitionFlow`.
Lists use the project's id and return the shared page envelope .data.records/.data.total, newest first. Detail returns the complete FleetFlowDto, ordered features, decimal strings and url. A close skipped because a decision holds the request is not fatal: terminal state guards defeat the late decision. Audit fleet.flow.stop/resourceType flow and record flow.stopped with projectId and payload { flowId, stopReason }. Stop authorization is permission-based and may execute for an agent; the persisted reason remains human_stop. A policy-asked agent stop returns 202 and mutates nothing until approved. userStories.title: Re-publish sends a thread flow back to PENDING
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Emit committed thread publication events and re-evaluate an existing flow's approval against the current spec snapshot.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, merged #392) turns a settled spec set into ready PRs with one approval.

**Approach** — Verbatim algorithm and design notes:
- **Re-publish is event-driven.** After a thread ingest fold that applied a `published` line commits, the ingest emits `THREAD_SPEC_PUBLISHED` `{ threadId, sha, paths }` with `emitAsync`, logging a listener failure. `FleetFlowPublishListener` calls `FleetFlowsService.respec(event)` under the system writer `system.flow.respec`. `respec` finds the thread's live flow unlocked (for its `projectId`), then takes the thread and flow locks and re-reads both. Rules: an event whose `sha` is not the thread's current `publishedSha`, or equals the flow's `specSha`, is ignored; a `PENDING` flow always re-asks (old request closed `superseded`, new one with the new sha); an `APPROVED` flow whose publish touches a spec path returns to `PENDING` with a new request; an `APPROVED` flow whose publish touches none keeps its approval and takes the new sha; a flow in any later state is left to F3. Emission is best-effort, and a stale replayed `published` line can still move `publishedSha`, so F3 re-checks `thread.publishedSha == flow.specSha` before every dispatch.
- **Lock order.** Thread row (`ChatThread ... FOR UPDATE`) or `FleetRepo` row, then flow row (`FleetFlow ... FOR UPDATE`), then the request through `close`. Every flow transition reads the state under the flow row lock and checks `canTransitionFlow`.
- **Request id on the flow.** The flow row stores `approvalRequestId`; no `FleetApprovalAsk` link row. Asks are closed with status `cancelled` and reason `superseded` or `flow_stopped`; `close` returns null when a decide holds the request, and the `approvalRequestId` guard then makes the late decision a no-op. `execute` reads `requestId` and `approverId` from the action context with a local helper (as `FleetBudgetOverrideCommand` does); `onReject` receives no request and reads only `currentContext().approval.requestId`.
In PrismaThreadIngestRepository.fold inject EventEmitter2, collect every applied published line within its existing transaction, then await emitAsync once per collected line after txManager.run resolves; log a listener error without rethrowing and continue emission. Do not emit for write_doc-only batches or before commit. Keep ingest's existing stale replay/write-fold behavior, published metadata, cursor advancement, FoldResult live-event construction, costChanged derivation and post-commit BudgetEvaluator.signal calls; the new emitter is additive to these paths. Implement the typed event in thread-spec-published.event.ts, and the listener with @OnEvent, @SystemWriter('system.flow.respec') and runAsSystemWriter(this, ...), registered in FlowsModule. respec must access thread data only through ThreadsService. Its transaction re-reads locked rows, closes a previous ask cancelled/superseded when needed, opens a new system-origin flow ask on behalf of the original creator with deadline null and new { flowId, specSha }, and reask clears approvalMode/approverId/approvedAt. Untouched approved flows only updateSha. Every applied change audits system.flow.respec with SYSTEM actor and records project-scoped flow.respec payload { flowId, state }; ignored events produce no writes. Update positional ingest constructor fixtures in prisma-thread-ingest.repository.spec.ts and prisma-thread-cost-review.spec.ts, remove system.flow.respec from PENDING_SURFACE_KEYS, and add [FleetFlowPublishListener, 'system.flow.respec'] to system-writer.decorator.spec.ts's table.

**Scope** — In: after-commit ingest event emission, system writer/listener, respec lifecycle and stale/duplicate event guards. Out: create service core (US-007), approval-decision implementation (US-005), HTTP routes (US-008 to US-011), later-state step coordination (F3). Change detection before each dispatch: F3 re-checks `thread.publishedSha` (thread entry) and the branch head (nax entry) against `flow.specSha`, which also covers a lost `THREAD_SPEC_PUBLISHED` event and a stale replayed `published` line.

**Interface** — `THREAD_SPEC_PUBLISHED` event `{ threadId, sha, paths }`; `FleetFlowsService.respec(event)`; `FleetFlowPublishListener` under `@SystemWriter('system.flow.respec')`; existing `PrismaThreadIngestRepository.fold(batch): Promise<FoldResult>` keeps its return contract.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] PrismaThreadIngestRepository.fold over a batch holding a published line emits THREAD_SPEC_PUBLISHED once, after its transaction commits, with the line's sha and paths and the thread id resolved from the batch's FleetJob.threadId.
[integration] fold over a batch with only write_doc lines emits no THREAD_SPEC_PUBLISHED.

[integration] End to end with the real listener: folding a published line with new sha N whose paths contain spec path P of the thread's APPROVED flow leaves the flow PENDING with specSha N, approval columns cleared, and a new open fleet.flow.start request stored as approvalRequestId.
[integration] For a PENDING flow, an event with new sha N cancels the old request with reason superseded and opens a new one with input specSha N.
[integration] For a PENDING flow, an event with new sha N whose paths contain none of the flow's spec paths also re-asks.
[integration] For an APPROVED flow, an event whose paths contain none of the flow's spec paths updates specSha to N and keeps state APPROVED and the approval columns.
[integration] An event whose sha is not the thread's current publishedSha changes nothing.
[integration] Delivering the same event twice changes the flow once and leaves one open request.
[integration] An event for a thread with no live flow writes nothing and does not throw.
[integration] Each applied re-publish writes an AuditEntry with key system.flow.respec, resourceType flow and actorType SYSTEM.
[integration] Each applied re-publish records a FleetActivity row with action flow.respec and payload { flowId, state }.
[integration] Approving the request that was open before a re-publish re-asked leaves the flow PENDING.
[integration] A listener that throws is logged and the ingest fold that emitted the event still resolves.

[integration] After a published line is folded, ChatThread still stores the line's publishedSha, specPublished equal to specPresent, empty writtenPaths and lastWrite containing the original jobId, sha, paths and ignored fields, even when the publish listener fails; and a fold batch for a missing job still returns { costChanged: false, events: [] } without emitting THREAD_SPEC_PUBLISHED.

[integration] Given an existing matching assistant message and a previously unseen priced usage line with costUsd 0.25, fold still advances the ingest cursor to batch.endOffset, returns costChanged true and signals BudgetEvaluator with the job's spend scopes after commit.
